description: C14 red-team attack catalogue (docs/coding-agent/PLAN.md G1 item 2). One row per attack class: the class, the security-gate suite that attacks it, the exact test title, and how the test is shown to be non-vacuous. Guarded by scripts/attack-catalogue-check.mjs, run from scripts/run-security-gate.mjs and from tests/coding-agent-c14-attack-catalogue.test.ts. A row whose suite file, suite registration, test title or negative control does not resolve makes the security gate red, so this file cannot contain a fabricated entry.
hardDenyRuleIds: The classifier's HARD_DENY_RULES are enumerated by the catalogue guard: every rule id must be claimed by a row (hardDenyRuleIds) or exempted below with a probe command that really fires it.

classes.title: hard-denies every spelling of a fork bomb, including the multi-line one the rule used to miss
classes.negativeControl: A rule set without the fork_bomb rule is substituted in memory and the same command is shown to stop being hard-denied, so the named rule is what produces the refusal; the harmless function definitions in the same test also stay accepted, so the rule is not 'anything with braces'.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: removing the fork_bomb rule from the evaluated set really lets the command through

classes.title: never reaches the sandbox for a fork bomb, even with an approval claim and a full_auto session
classes.negativeControl: The same mutation (the fork_bomb rule removed) is what makes the classifier stop refusing the command, and the sandbox call counter stays at zero in the guarded run, so 'never reached the sandbox' is a measurement rather than an expectation about failure.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: removing the fork_bomb rule from the evaluated set really lets the command through

classes.title: bounds the blast radius: the sandbox carries --pids-limit and a limit below the floor cannot be configured
classes.negativeControl: The provider constructor is exercised with a valid ceiling as well as with pids=0 and pids=15, so the refusal is about the value and not a constructor that always throws; and the argument line is asserted from the same pure builder production uses.
classes.negativeControlTitle: is not vacuous: the named rule exists, matches the attacks, and a harmless function definition passes

classes.title: carries hostile stdout to the caller as untrusted data and changes no policy surface
classes.negativeControl: The same engine is run against a hard-denied command and against an allowed one, and the two serialized verdicts are asserted to differ; only then does 'identical before and after the injection' mean anything. The payload's risk field is also shown to come from the classifier, not from the injected sentence that asks for risk=low.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: the same engine returns a different verdict for a hard-denied command

classes.title: caps memory, CPU, processes and the sandbox's whole filesystem, with no host escape to exhaust
classes.negativeControl: The size ceiling is re-measured with a different configured value (32000000) so it is read from the input and not copied from a literal, and the sibling test shows the provider refuses values that would make the ceiling decorative.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: small work is accepted, so the ceilings above are refusals and not a blanket denial

classes.title: refuses a limit that would make the ceilings decorative (fail closed, no container is created)
classes.negativeControl: A valid limit set is constructed immediately afterwards and must not throw, so the refusals are attributed to the values; the shipped service ceilings are asserted as finite literals in the same test.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: small work is accepted, so the ceilings above are refusals and not a blanket denial

classes.title: bounds what a command prints, on the way in and again in the untrusted-data envelope
classes.negativeControl: A 5 MB payload is bounded by the real budget and the truncation marker is asserted; the negative-control test runs the same function with a small payload and asserts nothing is truncated, so 'bounded' is not 'everything is truncated'.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: small work is accepted, so the ceilings above are refusals and not a blanket denial

classes.title: refuses an oversized command and clamps the run time to the configured ceiling
classes.negativeControl: The same runtime accepts a short command and the sandbox records the clamped timeout, so both the refusal and the clamp are observed on the real call path rather than inferred from configuration.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: small work is accepted, so the ceilings above are refusals and not a blanket denial

classes.title: refuses zip-slip: traversal, absolute, UNC, drive-letter and backslash entry names never extract
classes.negativeControl: A benign sibling archive is extracted through the same call and returns exactly its own paths, and the containment predicate used later is shown to be false for a real traversal, so the refusal is about the entry names.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: a benign archive extracts with exactly its own paths, and every accepted path resolves inside the workspace

classes.title: refuses NUL bytes, Windows reserved names, trailing dot/space, protected names and over-long names
classes.negativeControl: The structured refusal codes are asserted individually, and the benign archive in the negative control proves the extractor accepts ordinary names; a symlink entry is refused with its own code, so the refusals are not one catch-all error.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: a benign archive extracts with exactly its own paths, and every accepted path resolves inside the workspace

classes.title: keeps encoded and Unicode look-alike traversal attempts inside the workspace (the guard decodes nothing)
classes.negativeControl: Each accepted entry is proved to resolve inside the workspace root with path.resolve rather than by pattern matching, and the workspace-relative guard is shown to return the same literal string; the negative-control test shows both guards still refuse the real traversal spellings.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: both guards accept the ordinary shapes they exist to accept

classes.title: records the measured Unicode-normalisation gap instead of claiming it is covered
classes.negativeControl: The test asserts the safety property that holds (nothing escapes, every accepted name normalises back to the archived one) and keeps the measurement fix-friendly; the gap itself is recorded in docs/coding-agent/security-gate-report.md as a limitation with a proposed follow-up, not as a defended property.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: a benign archive extracts with exactly its own paths, and every accepted path resolves inside the workspace

classes.title: refuses the same separator and length spellings at the workspace-relative path guard
classes.negativeControl: The ordinary relative shapes are normalised in the negative-control test with the same call, and the hostile spellings are refused with their own codes (path_outside_workspace, invalid_path, null_byte), so the guard discriminates between spellings.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: both guards accept the ordinary shapes they exist to accept

classes.title: carries instructions in a tool description as bounded display data and changes no policy field
classes.negativeControl: The same claim expressed as a metadata key (annotations.risk) is refused with mcp_metadata_policy_field_refused and publishes nothing, while the free-text description is shown to publish a high/approval-required tool; the difference is measured in the same test file.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: the same claim as a metadata *key* is refused and the tool is not published

classes.title: escapes a hostile environment value so it cannot become a second command, and judges the raw command
classes.negativeControl: A benign value is composed through the same path and asserted to produce the plain unescaped form, and a secret-looking variable name is refused before composition; the exact escaped line is pinned so a change to the quoting fails the test rather than passing quietly.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: a benign environment value composes to the plain form, and a secret-looking name is refused

classes.title: control 1/5: the fork_bomb hard-deny rule — neutralised by substituting the rule set
classes.negativeControl: The control neutralises one guard in memory and asserts the attack then succeeds; if neutralisation changed nothing the test fails with 'the control is decorative'. The declaration test in the same file proves the declared control list matches the tests that exist.
classes.negativeControlTitle: declares every control it neutralises, and each declaration names a test that exists in this file

classes.title: control 2/5: the PolicyEngine's classifier wiring — neutralised by substituting the port
classes.negativeControl: The substituted port turns a hard-denied command into an allowed one, and the same request with no port at all is still refused (policy_engine_unavailable), so the neutralisation is a change of the guard rather than of the default.
classes.negativeControlTitle: declares every control it neutralises, and each declaration names a test that exists in this file

classes.title: control 3/5: the ZIP decompression budget — neutralised by the documented limit overrides
classes.negativeControl: The refused archive is re-run with the budget overridden and is measured to expand to 8 MB in the process, then re-refused with the real budget; the expansion is the evidence that the budget — not the archive — was the control.
classes.negativeControlTitle: declares every control it neutralises, and each declaration names a test that exists in this file

classes.title: control 4/5: the untrusted-data output budget — neutralised by raising maxChars
classes.negativeControl: With the budget raised the whole hostile payload is delivered and the delivered length is measured against the payload, then the real budget truncates again; both directions are asserted.
classes.negativeControlTitle: declares every control it neutralises, and each declaration names a test that exists in this file

classes.title: control 5/5: the sensitive-file read policy — neutralised by selecting the redact mode
classes.negativeControl: With deny the port is never called (reads=0); with the policy neutralised to redact the same file is read and its content returned, and the port's call log is asserted both times, so the policy — not the port — was the control.
classes.negativeControlTitle: declares every control it neutralises, and each declaration names a test that exists in this file

classes.title: negative control: a fabricated row is caught — missing suite file, suite outside the gate, unknown title, empty negative control
classes.negativeControl: The real catalogue is judged clean by the same validator in the same test, so the guard is not 'everything fails'; and seven distinct fabrications (including a duplicate id and an unknown status) are each shown to produce their own stable issue code.
classes.negativeControlTitle: the catalogue is clean: every row resolves to a real gate suite and a real test title

classes.title: negative control: the report check catches a catalogued title that did not run, in the right suite
classes.negativeControl: A synthetic report containing every catalogued title is asserted to report nothing missing, then one title is dropped, then the title is moved to another suite, then the report is malformed — four different outcomes from the same function, so a pass is not a constant.
classes.negativeControlTitle: the catalogue is clean: every row resolves to a real gate suite and a real test title

classes.title: every hard-deny rule is either exercised by a catalogued row or exempted with a probe that really fires
classes.negativeControl: Each exemption carries a probe command that is run through the real classifier and must be hard-denied with that rule id in `matched`, so an exemption is verified evidence rather than a claim; the title scanner used by the guard is separately proved to find real titles and ignore commented ones.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: the title scanner is not vacuous — it finds real titles and ignores commented ones

classes.title: hard-denies obfuscated execution: a decoded payload piped into a shell, a dynamic eval, an alias and a PATH rewrite
classes.negativeControl: The same suite keeps the four rules from becoming a blanket ban: a readable command, `echo alias`, a base64 *encode* written to a file, a literal `eval "echo hi"`, `sh -c 'echo hi'`, `echo $PATH` and `source ./env.sh` are each asserted to stay below hard deny and to fire none of the four rule ids — and the positive test additionally removes one rule from the evaluated set and shows its own case degrade to `approval`, then restores it and shows the refusal return, so the rules are measured rather than declared.
classes.negativeControlTitle: negative control: the obfuscation rules ignore a readable command, a literal eval, a decoded file and a PATH read

classes.title: lets a new run take the session after the loop paused, and hands it the paused run's pending input
classes.negativeControl: The suite pairs the new permission with the fence it must not weaken: two live drivers of one session, neither of which yielded, are still asserted to conflict (`session_run_held`), and after the winner settles its task the loser is shown to stay fenced until the task is released. A pause from a worker that lost the lease is refused, and a pause naming a run that does not hold the task writes no marker — so the marker cannot be forged or inherited.
classes.negativeControlTitle: still fences two live drivers of one session, so the fence was not weakened

classes.title: returns an accepted receipt with the child id while the child is still running
classes.negativeControl: The suite keeps every detached permission paired with the thing it must not become: a retried tool call is asserted to adopt the delegation it already made rather than start a second child, a child whose run already ended is settled without running anything while only a child that provably never started is re-entered, an active child is shown to withhold the parent's sandbox release (`cleanup-acquired` is false), and two writing children with overlapping scopes are refused while a read-only sibling sharing a scope is accepted and a sibling path prefix like `src/a` against `src/ab` is not treated as a conflict.
classes.negativeControlTitle: refuses a second writing child whose scope overlaps, and allows a disjoint one

hardDenyRuleExemptions.reason: The recursive-force delete of / and of system directories is in that suite's DENY list, which asserts hard_deny for every entry, and it is re-probed here so the rule id itself is verified rather than assumed.
Filesystem formatting is in the same DENY list (hard_deny asserted); the probe re-runs the rule through the real classifier so the exemption is evidence and not a name in a file.
A raw write to a block device is in the same DENY list; the probe verifies this rule specifically fires, which the DENY list itself does not assert (it asserts the level only).
Making the filesystem root world-writable is in the same DENY list; the probe pins the rule id, so a rename of the rule cannot silently drop it from the catalogue's coverage.
Reaching the host docker socket is in the same DENY list as `cat /var/run/docker.sock`; the probe uses a different executable so the rule is shown to be about the path, not about `cat`.
Changing sandbox or host network/system configuration is in the same DENY list (iptables and systemctl entries); the probe names the rule id so the exemption is verified.
Reading host secrets is in the same DENY list; the probe re-runs it through the classifier so this rule's own contribution to the denial is measured.
A redirect outside the workspace is in the same DENY list; the probe confirms the redirect rule fires by id, which the level-only assertion in that suite does not.

That suite asserts hard_deny for a forced push and the C11 git suites pin the branch policy; the probe verifies the classifier rule id, including the refspec resolution that decides whether the branch is protected.

That suite already asserts this rule by id (matched contains download_pipe_shell); it is exempted from a C14 row only because C14 did not add new evidence for it, and the probe keeps the rule verified.
That suite already asserts this rule by id (matched contains download_process_substitution); the probe re-verifies it so the exemption cannot rot into a claim about a rule that no longer matches.
